newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian budget seen adjusting oil duties - minister.
newsitem.headline: Indian budget seen adjusting oil duties - minister.

text.p: Indian Petroleum Minister T.R. Balu said he expects duties on petroleum products to be adjusted in the 1997/98 (April-March) budget, to be presented later on Friday to parliament.

"Let us see what happens, what is fixed, what relaxed duty structure is there in the budget. I expect some duty structure rationalisation," Balu told Asian News International (ANI), a local news agency.

Earlier Balu said the government had no plan to raise the domestic prices of petroleum products to stem a backlog of payments to state-owned oil firms, projected to reach 158 billion rupees by the end of March.

Oil analysts in Bombay recently said the government was expected to cut import tariffs for crude oil and might raise them for refined products in the 1997/98 budget, set to be presented by Finance Minister P. Chidambaram at 5 p.m. (1130 GMT).
If the differentials between crude and product tariffs were restructured, it would be a key step towards liberalising the refining industry, analysts said.
